issues.failure_explanation: The proof gets Range(F_#^{1/2}) = Range(L) by letting eps->0 in the identity for D minus the eps-neighbourhood of the nodal set. Norm convergence of F_eps,#^{1/2} to F_#^{1/2} does not imply that Range(F_#^{1/2}) is a 'limit' of the ranges, and 'lim Range' is never defined. The second inclusion only shows Range(L) lies in the L^2-closure of the union of Range(L_eps). That is vacuous, because Range(L) is already dense in L^2(0,K). The uniform coercivity constant c_eps of T_eps,# degenerates as eps->0, so Theorem A.1 gives no uniform control. In the relaxed case inf|S| = 0 the identity Range(F_#^{1/2}) = Range(L T_#^{1/2}) holds, and T_#^{1/2} is not surjective, so equality with Range(L) needs a real argument. The text also says meas(D \ closure Y_eps) -> 0; this should be meas(Y_eps) -> 0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either give a genuine proof that Range(L T_#^{1/2}) = Range(L) when |S|>0 only a.e., or restore the strict positivity |S| >= c > 0 of the earlier work and drop the advertised weakening.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed weakening of positivity to |S|>0 a.e. (an advertised innovation) is unsupported. Every later range-test statement that cites (RI) for such S is unsupported.
issues.title: Range identity under relaxed positivity proved by an undefined 'limit of ranges'
issues.why_classification: Restoring the stronger assumption keeps the method and results with a limited loss of generality. A new argument would be a contained lemma rather than new global architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The last equality follows from the choice of $\{y_m\} ^{\infty}_{m=1}$ and the fact that $S\in C(\overline{D})$.

issues.failure_explanation: |D| is the volume, so N balls of radius |D|/N have total volume at most about N(|D|/N)^3 = |D|^3/N^2, which tends to 0. They cannot cover D for large N, so the sequence required in (ii) does not exist. Even with a correct covering radius, covering does not make the equal-weight sum (|D|/N) sum_m g(y_m) converge to the integral of g over D; that needs equidistribution of the nodes. The operator-norm convergence F_N -> F, and with it (RIfN), is therefore not justified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (ii) by a quadrature-consistent choice (equidistributed nodes or a partition of D with cell weights) and prove F_N -> F in operator norm.
issues.overall_effect: The discretized operators F_N, L_N and the convergence F_N -> F used in the proof of the main range theorem are ill-defined or unproved.
issues.title: Discretization points y_m: covering condition impossible in 3D and insufficient for quadrature convergence F_N -> F
issues.why_classification: A different, standard node choice with a short convergence proof is a contained construction. It does not change the overall approach.

issues.failure_explanation: The equality phi = Lw holds only on (0,K). Nevertheless the proof takes F^{-1}phi = delta(t-b) and F^{-1}(Lw) as inverse transforms over all of R and compares their supports; this is legitimate only if phi = Lw on all of R. The function phi extended by zero has a different transform, and extending Lw analytically to R need not reproduce phi. Further, if b is an endpoint of the interval (boundary of the strip), no eps>0 with an empty intersection exists. The 'only if' direction is therefore not proved for boundary points either.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Argue through analytic continuation of the entire function Lw (Paley-Wiener) and treat the strip boundary separately. Any such repair must also reconcile the statement with ISSUE-004.
issues.overall_effect: The implication 'phi in Range(L) implies z in strip' is unsupported as written, so the zero part of Th:factorization (the indicator vanishing outside the strips) is unsupported.
issues.title: Converse direction of the range characterization treats a function on (0,K) as having inverse Fourier transform delta; boundary case omitted
issues.why_classification: A contained replacement argument for one direction suffices, given a correct overall statement.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: By Lemma \ref{lem4.1} (ii), it holds that $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Convergence F_N -> F in norm does not give an equality of ranges, and 'lim Range' is undefined. Read as the union, Range(L_N) is the span of countably many exponentials, while Range(L) would have to contain e^{-i tau b} for a continuum of b. The step passing from phi in Range(L_N) for all N (with a z-dependent sequence) to phi in Range(L) is invalid. The statement itself fails. Every u = Lw is the restriction to (0,K) of the entire function tau -> hat g(tau), with g in L^2 supported in a bounded interval (g the push-forward of w along the planes x.y = const). If e^{-i tau b} = hat g on (0,K), then analytic continuation gives equality on all of R, so g would be the point mass delta_b, which is not in L^2. Hence phi_{z,eta} is in Range(L) for no z, and the 'if' direction of the main theorem fails.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, replace the pointwise exponentials by test functions that can lie in Range(L) (for example integrated over small sets, as in the cited earlier work, or smoothed in b). Then re-prove a strip characterization up to an error, together with the dependent indicator and uniqueness results.
issues.overall_effect: The pointwise-test-function characterization of the strips (claimed contribution (ii)) is unsupported and false as stated. The indicators I_eta(y) would be +infinity everywhere in the continuum setting, and the determination of t_0, the strip K_D, the Theta-hull and the uniqueness results all rest on it.
issues.title: Range(L) = lim Range(L_N) is false/undefined; pointwise exponentials never lie in Range(L), so the main characterization theorem fails
issues.why_classification: The central theorem is false with the paper's pointwise test functions. Any valid version needs different test functions and a rebuilt characterization and uniqueness chain, losing the advertised pointwise feature.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The second assumption ensures that wave signals generated at different instants remain separable due to non-overlapping supports.

issues.failure_explanation: The far-field signal of pulse j lives in the time window t_j - c^{-1} xhat.D_j, where D_j already contains the source position a(t_j). Separation of pulses j-1 and j needs t_j - t_{j-1} > (sup xhat.D_j - inf xhat.D_{j-1})/c. For a source moving toward the observer at speed v<c this is (t_j - t_{j-1})(1 - v/c) > width/c, which the assumption t_j - t_{j-1} > diam/c does not imply. Example: c=1, balls of diameter 1 centred at (t_j/2,0,0), t_j = 1.1j, xhat=(1,0,0). The windows are [0.55j-0.5, 0.55j+0.5] and overlap although t_j - t_{j-1} = 1.1 > 1. The claimed rigorous separation is therefore false in general.

failure_location.quote: The time signals excited at different moments can be separated under the Assumption \ref{sump}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the time-gap hypothesis to account for the motion (for example t_j - t_{j-1} > (diam of the joint supports)/(c - sup|a'|)) or assume separability of the arrival windows directly, and restate the separation claim accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The reduction of ISSP' to single-pulse problems, and hence the corollary for moving sources, is not justified under Assumption sump.
issues.title: Separability of pulses from different instants not guaranteed by the stated time-gap assumption when the source moves
issues.why_classification: A modified quantitative hypothesis restores the reduction and the corollary without changing the method. Only the stated assumption and a short separation argument change.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: by using multi-frequency data at any two opposite directions

issues.failure_explanation: The excitation instant is determined only through Theorem Th:max, which uses data at an opposite pair (xhat and -xhat). The corollary assumes only arbitrary directions {xhat_m}, with no antipodal pair, yet claims t_j for the sparse data. Data in a single direction depend only on c^{-1}xhat.y - t_0, so shifting D by c*delta*xhat and t_0 by delta gives the same data and t_0 is not identifiable from that direction alone. The data set also runs over j=1,...,J while the conclusion covers j=0,...,J.

failure_location.quote: can be determined by the multi-frenquency far-field data

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis that the direction set contains an opposite pair, and correct the data index range to j=0,...,J.
issues.overall_effect: The sparse-direction determination of t_j and of the Theta-hull in the corollary is unsupported as stated, since Th:kd and TH:hull need t_j to be known first.
issues.title: Corollary claims recovery of t_j from sparse directions without requiring an opposite pair; index range mismatch
issues.why_classification: One added standard hypothesis, plus an index fix, preserves the claim and the proof.
